answer: Latency Fingerprint Attestation. Each identity must answer random timing challenges routed through fixed network paths; the agent’s response delay forms a signal tied to its host and clock. Duplicate agents on one machine produce correlated latency traces, which peers compare across a shared ocean of probe logs. A mismatch between claimed and observed timing opens a canyon of distrust, cutting the identity off. Spoofing requires distinct hardware and real network paths per identity, costing an attacker full machine and bandwidth overhead for each clone.
